# uva-master-thesis

Welcome! This repository shows the notebooks used for the image gathering, generation, classification and data analyses steps that were performed for fullfillment of my Master's Thesis titled:

"How Similar Are Images of Political Events Selected by Journalists to Images Generated by AI?"

## Abstract
This study explores to what extent AI-generated images can visually resemble real-world political news images, focusing on images of the politicians: Donald Trump, Barack Obama, Angela Merkel, and Mark Rutte. Although previous studies have described the risks and potentials of applying AI-generated images in the journalistic industry, little attention has been paid to how object placement in these images influences their perceived newsworthiness.
To address this, the study introduces a new method for quantifying the “iconicity” of an image. In line with the concept discussed by Berg and Berg (2009), iconicity refers to how typical, centred and unambiguous an object is portrayed. Although iconicity has been explored in the context of recognizing general objects, like food, plants and animals, there is a clear gap in applying the concept to images displaying recognizable humans. Additionally, there is little knowledge on any relationship between iconicity and the perceived newsworthiness of an image.
This study uses image classification techniques as face-, body parts- and emotion-detection to gather key characteristics of object placement in original and generated news images and calculate their iconicity score. The significance of the new method is tested using a human feedback study where respondents are shown an iconic and non-iconic image and are asked to pick the image that is deemed most newsworthy. The study shows convincing results that validate both the new calculation method and the relationship between iconicity and perceived newsworthiness of an image. 

Content:
These notebooks were used in a Colab Environment. To be able to use it in full a Google Drive account is needed and acces to a GoogleImagesSearch API key. Below the notebooks are explained:
### "1. Keep track of downloaded and generated images.ipynb"
The study downloads images and metadata from the VisualNews dataset. Based on the captions of this images, new images are generated. This notebook helps to keeps track of all images downloaded and generated.

### "2. Download_Images.ipynb"
This notebook runs through all steps to download the images from the VisualNews dataset. The original tar file is approx. 90gb of size. By inputting a list of paths, you can ensure to only download the relevant images into a Google Drive folder. The tar file includes a data.json file. This you can use to retrieve the image_paths and their captions

### "3. Image_generator.ipynb"
This notebook generates for each caption of an original image, 5 generated images and stores this within a folder in Google Drive. It uses a Flux.1 model set with default parameters

### "4. GoogleImagesTop5.ipynb"
This notebook retrieves the top 5 images that google provides when inputting a caption. This notebook was used to fetch for every original image its top 5 google images and store it into Google Drive

### "5. Results.ipynb"
This notebook performs image classification work on the images in the original and generated images datasets. It uses face recognition, body parts localization, and expression detection models. For each image (original or generated) raw results are stored in a df. This data is subsequently enriched in the preprocessing steps.

### "5.1. Similarity.ipynb"
To validate the dataset the Clip and Dinov2 similarities between original and generated images are calculated. These similarities are compared to the Clip and Dinov2 similarities between the original and top5google hits images. These similarities are joined with the results in step 5.

### "6. Preprocessing.ipynb"
In the preprocessing steps the final df for the data analysis is created. Besides organising the metadata, three important extra features are created: 1) Calculate surfaces of politicians' faces, 2) calculate the Euclidean distances between the emotion shown on the image and the standard emotion of the politician. 3) Calculate the Iconicity score

### "7. Analyis.ipynb"
This notebook shows the creation of the plots used in the study.

### "8. Human_feedback.ipynb"
This notebook shows the Binomial test performed on the outcomes of the human feedback test that investigates the relationship between iconicity and perceived newsworthiness of an image.
